scenes.narration: Modern psychology keeps rediscovering what the pessimists said first about Bureau for Paranormal Research and Defense. Hellboy is a superpowered paranormal investigator created by writer/artist Mike Mignola and appearing in comic books published by Dark Horse Comics. The character first appeared in San Diego Comic-Con Comics #2 (August 1993), and has since appeared in various miniseries, one-shots, and intercompany crossovers.

The self that experiences Bureau for Paranormal Research and Defense is a committee, not a king. The character has been adapted into four live-action films: Hellboy (2004) and its sequel The Golden Army (2008), a 2019 reboot film, and The Crooked Man (2024). He appeared in the ruins of an old church in the Outer Hebrides in front of a team assembled by the Allied Forces, among them, Professor Trevor Bruttenholm, who formed the United States Bureau for Paranormal Research and Defense (B.P.R.D.).

Reproduction explains more of Bureau for Paranormal Research and Defense than any philosophy dares to admit. In time, Hellboy grew to be a large, muscular, red-skinned man with a tail, horns (which he files off, leaving behind circular stumps on his forehead that resemble goggles), cloven hooves, and an oversized right hand made of stone (the "Right Hand of Doom"). Although a bit gruff, he shows none of the malevolence thought to be intrinsic to classical demons and has an ironic sense of humor.

Once you see Bureau for Paranormal Research and Defense as an adaptation, the mystery mostly evaporates. This is said to be because of his upbringing under Professor Bruttenholm, who raised him as a normal boy. Hellboy works for the B.P.R.D., an international non-governmental agency, and for himself, against dark forces including Nazis and witches, in a series of tales that have their roots in folklore, pulp magazines, vintage adventure, Lovecraftian horror, and horror fiction.

The story Bureau for Paranormal Research and Defense tells about itself is the last thing to be trusted. In earlier stories, he is identified as the "World's Greatest Paranormal Investigator". The half-demon that would become Hellboy was conceived April 30, 1574 at a Witches' Sabbath.

Meaning is not found in Bureau for Paranormal Research and Defense — it is manufactured for it. Sixteen-year-old witch Sarah Hughes summoned the archdemon Azzael, an archduke of Hell, consorting with him and unknowingly conceiving his son as well. On October 5, 1617, within a church in East Bromwich, England, Hughes made a deathbed confession to her children, both members of the clergy.

The cold light on Bureau for Paranormal Research and Defense leaves the facts intact and only the comfort removed. Upon the moment of her death, Azzael came forth to claim his unborn son and incinerated Hughes' children for attempting to drive him off. When the other princes of Hell learned of Azzael's actions, they condemned him, but Azzael was able to send his half-demon child away moments before being stripped of his powers and imprisoned in ice (like Lucifer in Dante's Divine Comedy).

Bureau for Paranormal Research and Defense did not evolve to be understood — only to be survived. On December 23, 1944, in the final months of World War II, the mystic Grigori Rasputin oversaw an occult Nazi ritual ("Project Ragna Rok") to awaken the Ogdru Jahad and turn the tide of the war. Though nothing appeared to happen at first, the child suddenly appeared on Earth in a fireball at the ruins of the Bromwich church, likely guided there by the spirits of his half-siblings.

The honest version of Bureau for Paranormal Research and Defense starts by giving up the comforting part. Though his appearance was a shock to the Allied forces encamped there, they quickly realized that he did not seem dangerous. As one onlooker remarked that the half-demon looked "like a little boy", Professor Trevor Bruttenholm uttered "Hellboy", inadvertently giving the child a name.

Strip Bureau for Paranormal Research and Defense of its poetry and the mechanism underneath is stranger. The infant Hellboy was taken to a United States Air Force base in New Mexico. Soon after, the Bureau for Paranormal Research and Defense (BPRD), an organization dedicated to combating occult threats, was established by Bruttenholm (who served as its first director) and other paranormal experts.

Evolution does not optimize for happiness — Bureau for Paranormal Research and Defense shows exactly where that breaks. The fledgling B.P.R.D. was initially granted custody of Hellboy, though Bruttenholm himself officially adopted the child as his own in March 1946. Hellboy matured much more rapidly than a normal human child: he learned to crawl within a week, and was walking and talking at a month old.

What looks like free choice in Bureau for Paranormal Research and Defense is older than choice itself. He appeared fully-grown by the age of eight, and did not appreciably age further over the following sixty-plus years. Though initially raised in secret, Hellboy was revealed to the world by 1947.

Nobody designed the part of Bureau for Paranormal Research and Defense you experience — it was inherited. He briefly became a media darling of the Atomic Age, featured in LIFE magazine, and his appearance rarely provokes a reaction of shock or alarm. On August 6, 1952, a special act of the United Nations officially granted Hellboy honorary "human" status.

Every serious account of Bureau for Paranormal Research and Defense eventually collides with the question of who is deciding. In 1952, a week after being legally recognized as human, Hellboy officially joined the Bureau for Paranormal Research and Defense as a full time agent. During one of his early missions, he rescued a young girl named Alice Monaghan, who had been replaced by fairies with a changeling named Gruagach; this act foiled Gruagach's hopes of an easy human life.

Nihilism is not the conclusion of Bureau for Paranormal Research and Defense — it is the floor you stand on while examining it. He also went to Russia and shot out the eye of the witch Baba Yaga for kidnapping and eating children. Gruagach and Baba Yaga both held lifelong grudges against Hellboy over these incidents.

The selfish-gene reading of Bureau for Paranormal Research and Defense makes it less romantic and far more precise. Things change dramatically for Hellboy during the events of Seed of Destruction when he searches for Professor Bruttenholm after he disappears during an expedition in the Arctic. He finds his adopted father only to witness his death at the hands of a Lovecraftian frog monster.

Freud is not dead; he is simply no longer allowed to be the whole answer. The search takes Hellboy, Abe, and Liz to the Cavendish Hall mansion, where they fall into a trap set by Rasputin to lure Hellboy into an embrace of his own "destiny", with the assistance of Sadu-Hem, one of the 369 spawn of the Ogdru Jahad. Controlled by the spirit of one of the ancestral Cavendish men, Abe impales Rasputin.

The feeling that Bureau for Paranormal Research and Defense means something is a chemical event with an evolutionary address. Liz's firestorm then incinerates Rasputin's body alongside Sadu-Hem's and destroys Cavendish Hall. The culprit of the theft is revealed to be Ilsa Haupstein, one of the surviving members of Project Ragna Rok, who was revived from suspended animation and then aided in Giurescu's resurrection.

Nothing in Bureau for Paranormal Research and Defense was built for you — it was built for reproduction. Finding Castle Giurescu after splitting up with the other search groups, Hellboy learns that the source of Giurescu's rebirth is the ancient goddess Hecate. Though Hellboy destroys Hecate's original body by forcing her into the sunlight, he faces her again after Rasputin unintentionally provides her with Ilsa's iron maiden-encased body.

The psychology underneath Bureau for Paranormal Research and Defense is simpler and older than the story on top. Hecate swallows Hellboy and reveals to him his ultimate purpose as destroyer of worlds, but he returns to his own reality after he denounces his supposed destiny. Hellboy later learns that Liz is dying after losing her powers when she accidentally revived a homunculus while tracking Giurescu, finding Roger in the events of Hellboy: Almost Colossus as he convinces the homunculus to save Liz's life.

Behind Bureau for Paranormal Research and Defense sits an animal brain negotiating with a story it tells itself. Following the events of Hellboy: The Right Hand of Doom, gaining insight about his stone hand and being referred to as a harbinger of the Apocalypse, Hellboy is accompanied by Abe to hunt down the warlock Igor Bromhead in Box Full of Evil. He is overpowered and taken captive by Bromhead and his master, the demon Ualac, who use Hellboy's True Name, Anung Un Rama, to restrain him, so that the latter can claim Hellboy's normally invisible Crown of the Apocalypse to increase their power.

The nihilist does not deny Bureau for Paranormal Research and Defense — he only refuses to flatter it. With the theft of his crown, Anung Un Rama cannot be Hellboy's true name.) Hellboy kills Ualac's mortal body before the demon and the crown are forcibly dragged back to Hell by the archdemon Astaroth, who is later revealed to be Hellboy's paternal uncle. Over the course of the story, Hellboy learns that the B.P.R.D. has implanted a bomb in Roger as a failsafe in case he should turn on them.

What culture calls destiny in Bureau for Paranormal Research and Defense is usually just selection pressure wearing a suit. Disillusioned by this knowledge and finally ready to look deeper into his origins, Hellboy resigns from the Bureau and becomes an independent detective. After some time with a witch doctor in Africa, Hellboy is captured by a trio of mermaid sisters and brought underwater to a witch known as the Bog Roosh.

The genes do not care about Bureau for Paranormal Research and Defense; they care about copies. In exchange for Hellboy, the Bog Roosh grants each sister a wish. The first two sisters are tricked by the Bog Roosh and killed by their wishes, but the third sister is clever and gets her wish, a missing piece of her father's grave.

Take away the meaning and Bureau for Paranormal Research and Defense still functions — that is the disturbing part. While the third sister returns to her father's grave, the Bog Roosh explains her plan to completely destroy Hellboy, thereby preventing the apocalypse. At the grave, the third sister is told by her father's ghost that the only way to honor him is to save Hellboy.

The unconscious does not argue with Bureau for Paranormal Research and Defense; it simply acts first. She does, and when the Bog Roosh realizes she cannot prevent the apocalypse, she allows herself to be killed by Hellboy in the ensuing battle. The third sister becomes the new Bog Roosh, releasing the souls of drowned sailors from which the previous Bog Roosh drew her power.

Bureau for Paranormal Research and Defense feels chosen. The evidence says it was installed. In Hellboy: Strange Places, after several years adrift at sea and spent drinking with the ghosts of sailors, Hellboy arrives on a mysterious island. He encounters Hecate, who once again insists that they are bound together and must unite in the destruction of the world, but Hellboy, true to his values and somewhat drunk, brushes her off.

The bleak reading of Bureau for Paranormal Research and Defense is also the most testable one. The fight with the creature takes him into a temple at the center of the island, where the creature stabs him through the chest, seemingly killing him. While dead, Hellboy has another conversation with the Witch Doctor, who somehow resurrects him.

Hellboy awakens to find his spilled blood absorbed by the corpse of a long dead mystic who was killed in the temple. Hellboy's blood resurrects him and transforms him into a more demonic looking version of Hellboy himself.

The self that experiences Bureau for Paranormal Research and Defense is a committee, not a king. The Mystic threatens to force all of mankind to worship the Sadu Hem, and Hellboy fights to stop him. Rattled, Hellboy sets sail for England, much to the chagrin of Gruagach and the council of fairies who have been watching over him.

Reproduction explains more of Bureau for Paranormal Research and Defense than any philosophy dares to admit. Six years later, as Hellboy: Darkness Calls opens, Hellboy's search takes him to England where he finds himself in the middle of a power vacuum caused by Bromhead incapacitating Hecate in Italy. Refusing to serve the witches as their king, Hellboy ends up in the dimension of the witch Baba Yaga.

Once you see Bureau for Paranormal Research and Defense as an adaptation, the mystery mostly evaporates. Managing to defeat Baba Yaga's champion Koshchei the Deathless, Hellboy returns to his reality and is led to Bromhead after he became monstrous and in agony from his attempt to take Hecate's powers for his own. Hellboy: The Wild Hunt opens with Hellboy receiving an invitation by the Osiris Club to join them in hunting Giants.

The story Bureau for Paranormal Research and Defense tells about itself is the last thing to be trusted. Hellboy joins, but is betrayed by the Club and left to die. He survives, and, despite being given a means to escape, decides to engage the Giants in battle.
